Let’s dive into Chapter 2: Overcoming Excuses and Facing the Realities of Time.
Now that you’ve started to see just how valuable your time really is, there’s another hurdle that often stands in the way—excuses. I’m sure you’ve heard them, and maybe even used a few yourself. Things like, “I’m just too busy,” or “There’s no way I can fit anything else into my day.” With work, family, and all those never-ending chores, it can feel like you’re stretched way too thin to carve out any time for yourself.
But here’s the thing—most of the time, that feeling isn’t quite accurate. If you break down a typical day, sure, work might eat up a big chunk. But there are still hours left unaccounted for. Think about your commute, the time you spend making dinner, or those quiet moments before bed. So much of that time slips by in passive activities—like scrolling through social media, flipping through the news, or just zoning out in front of the TV.
The real challenge isn’t about finding more hours—it’s about setting your intentions. It’s so easy to let your routines take over, letting the day just flow by on autopilot. It’s kind of like being on a river without a paddle, just letting the current decide where you’ll end up. But what if you grabbed the rudder and started steering? What if you chose where you wanted to go?
Facing the realities of time means being honest—really honest—about where your hours are slipping away. That can feel a little uncomfortable, especially when you start noticing patterns of procrastination or just avoiding things you know could help you grow. But trust me, this honest self-check is where real change starts. Try tracking how you spend your day, even just for a week. You’ll probably be surprised at how much time is actually up for grabs.
Now, let’s talk about some of those classic excuses:
Maybe you think you need big, uninterrupted blocks of time to work on yourself. Or, you feel so wiped out after work that anything extra seems impossible. Or perhaps you believe personal growth is only for people with special talents or fancy resources.
Here’s something to remember—none of these excuses hold up under a closer look. Even tiny pockets of time, used regularly, can add up to real progress. The right activities—whether it’s reading, reflecting, or learning something new—can actually boost your energy, not drain it. And when it comes to growth, it’s your willingness to learn and stick with it that matters most—not some mythical, natural talent.
So, facing these excuses head-on and really examining how your days are structured—that’s how you start to spot opportunities for change. It all begins with a little honesty and a willingness to take ownership of your time. That self-awareness? It’s your ticket to more freedom, more fulfillment, and a life that feels a whole lot more intentional.
